\section*{Technical memo: the Tencent stake under IAS 28}

\subsection*{1. The accounting: standard and measurement}
% - IAS 28 equity method: cost + share of profit/OCI - dividends. Significant influence
%   presumed at >=20% (IAS 28.5); Prosus's chair sits on Tencent's board.\footnote{...p.86}
% - Carrying value 42,172 = share of Tencent net assets 35,547 + goodwill 6,625; quoted
%   (Level 1) value 127,637.
% - Lag: Tencent Dec year-end, Prosus March; up to 3-month lag with adjustments for
%   significant events (note 3). Auditor's key audit matter.
% - Partial disposals: proceeds less proportionate carrying value = gain; 4.7bn in FY2026
%   on 95.6m shares sold for 6.5bn. Tencent's buy-backs create "goodwill" inside the
%   carrying amount (2,354 in FY2024 -> 6,625 in FY2026).
% - No deferred tax: distributions "do not have tax consequences".
% - Impairment: IAS 28.40-43 via IAS 36 on the whole investment; 85bn headroom.

\subsection*{2. Where judgement and estimation enter}
% - Significant influence at 22.66% and falling 0.83 pp/yr -> 20% in ~3.2 years; not listed
%   among critical judgements (note 3). IAS 28.6 indicators: board seat yes, the rest no.
% - If lost (IAS 28.22): remeasure to fair value, ~85bn one-off gain; then IFRS 9. Prosus's
%   FY2026 precedent (Delivery Hero) was FVOCI,\footnote{FY2026 AR, note 6, p.~150.} so
%   afterwards only dividends (~1.2bn) would reach profit.
% - Lag-period adjustments: "significant judgement" (note 3, p.145); size undisclosed.
% - Core headline earnings: Tencent 8,117 of 8,340 (97%), after adding back Tencent's

% - Impairment indicators judged against market price and consensus (audit committee p.59).
